paragraph: Angola Telecom's executive director [said in July 2026](<https://pti.ao/angola-telecom-preve-operacao-do-cabo-submarino-sarssy-ate-2027/>) that a terrestrial fibre link joins Santa Clara in Angola to Namibia and carries services of Angola Telecom and Telecom Namibia in both directions. In the last twelve months, the two companies also [signed a memorandum in March 2026](<https://pti.ao/angola-telecom-preve-operacao-do-cabo-submarino-sarssy-ate-2027/>) for the SARSSy sea cable. Angola's and Mozambique's ministers [signed one on 22 June 2026](<https://www.oeconomico.com/mocambique-e-angola-avancam-com-cabo-nacala-lobito-para-reforcar-corredor-digital-regional/>) for a Nacala to Lobito cable. In November 2026 the communications minister [put the SARSSy cable at the study and preparation stage](<https://pp.itu.int/2026/en/itu_policy_statements/angola/>). No exchange point or data centre shared with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Burundi's Council of Ministers [adopted a memorandum on 8 May 2024](<https://abpinfo.bi/2024/05/15/un-memorandum-dentente-du-projet-dinterconnexion-par-fibre-optique-entre-la-republique-democratique-du-congo-et-le-burundi-a-ete-adopte-au-conseil-des-ministres/>) for a fibre interconnection with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which the government calls a joint initiative. Burundi's and Zambia's ministers [signed a memorandum in Lusaka in October 2024](<https://itweb.africa/article/burundi-zambia-agree-underwater-fibre-connection/kLgB17ezr59M59N4>) for a fibre cable under Lake Tanganyika. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The report on the Zambia cable says an unnamed private firm was contracted, and no source names a contract or a start of works on either link. No shared link, exchange point or data facility has been found in service. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

Benin's state infrastructure company SBIN, with CSquared and the Nigerian operator Phase3, [announced a fibre route from Lagos to Accra in May 2025](<https://csquared.com/csquared-phase3-and-sbin-commission-lagos-to-accra-terrestrial-fibre-route-strengthening-west-africas-digital-resilience/>), running through Benin, Togo and Ghana. The partners said it was configured, activated and tested, and gave no date for it to enter service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Benin lies on a [Lagos to Dakar route that Phase3 and Sonatel activated in 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/05/09/west-africas-digital-backbone-phase3-and-sonatel-launch-3500km-fibre-route/>), but no Beninese party to it has been found. No source found says the Lagos to Accra route has entered service. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

WACREN, the regional research and education network, [said in 2025 that FasoREN's connection to its regional network was still partial](<https://indico.wacren.net/event/256/>). FasoREN is Burkina Faso's national research network, and the connection runs over national fibre laid by ANPTIC, the state digital agency. [In November 2025 WACREN held a workshop in Ouagadougou](<https://indico.wacren.net/event/256/>) to set a roadmap and timetable for joining FasoREN fully to the regional backbone. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found, and no source says the research network connection is complete. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

In May 2025 BoFiNet's acting chief executive [said it has fibre connections to all of Botswana's neighbours](<https://www.bwtechzone.com/2025/05/how-bofinet-plans-to-transform-botswana.html>). The source names no party in those countries. In the last twelve months, Namibia's MTC and BoFiNet [signed a memorandum in February 2026](<https://thebrief.com.na/2026/02/mtc-bofinet-sign-agreement-to-strengthen-namibia-botswana-digital-connectivity/>) on cross-border fibre interconnection, IP transit and wholesale capacity. BoFiNet [says the two had recently completed cross-border fibre interconnections](<https://www.bofinet.co.bw/index.php/news/article/bofinet-signs-mou-with-mtc-namibia-to-further-bolster-connectivity-reliability-for-botswana>) at Mamuno to Charles Hill and at Ngoma. No source found says those interconnections carry traffic, or that a shared link, exchange point or data facility is in service. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

The Central African Republic [inaugurated its national backbone on 6 February 2023](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/infrastructures/0802-105283-inauguration-de-la-dorsale-optique-nationale-de-la-republique-centrafricaine-et-de-l-interconnexion-avec-le-congo>), with links to Cameroon at Gamboula and to Congo at Bomassa. The African Development Bank [closed the project in September 2023](<https://www.afdb.org/fr/news-and-events/les-jeunes-centrafricains-formes-aux-metiers-du-numerique-grace-la-fibre-optique-installee-avec-lappui-de-la-banque-africaine-de-developpement-et-de-lunion-europeenne-69893>) with both links built. In the last twelve months, vandalism in March 2026 [partly cut national service](<https://sunvimedia.info/vers-une-diversification-de-la-connectivite-en-centrafrique/>), and in October 2026 the two routes [were still the country's fibre links abroad](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/1210-142321-internet-qu-est-ce-que-la-liaison-par-fibre-avec-la-rdc-peut-apporter-a-la-centrafrique>). No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Côte d'Ivoire's and Guinea's digital ministers [signed a protocol in Conakry on 11 October 2024](<https://www.gouv.ci/actualite/cooperation-deux-importants-protocoles-daccord-signes-entre-les-gouvernements-ivoirien-et-guineen-dans-le-secteur-numerique-2384>) to interconnect the two countries' fibre networks. No source reports works begun on it. In the last twelve months, the country's use of RASCOM, the satellite organisation of African states, was cited and not changed: its director general [said on 31 July 2026](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2643635/culture/communication-satellitaire-la-cote-divoire-mise-sur-rascom-pour-accelerer-la-couverture-numerique-du-territoire>) that its services are already used in Côte d'Ivoire. He cited the state broadcaster RTI, which used RASCOM capacity during the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations. No Ivorian party to a cross-border fibre link in service has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

The Central African Republic [inaugurated its backbone in February 2023](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/infrastructures/0802-105283-inauguration-de-la-dorsale-optique-nationale-de-la-republique-centrafricaine-et-de-l-interconnexion-avec-le-congo>), interconnected with Cameroon at Gamboula. Chad told ITU-D in March 2026 that its [link to CAMTEL's network is working](<https://www.itu.int/md/D26-SG01-C-0040/en>). In the last twelve months, Gabon's SPIN and Cameroon's CAMTEL [signed a memorandum on CAB-Corridor](<https://spin.ga/cab-corridor-spin-camtel-connectivite-afrique-centrale/>), published in October 2026, that would join Cameroon, Gabon and Congo. Chad's regulator [suspended a planned operator route from N'Djamena](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/fiber-networking/chad-tells-operators-to-fast-track-fiber-link-to-cameroon>) in February 2026. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Congo's SOCOF and Tanzania's TTCL [made the Kalemie to Kigoma lake cable official on 20 October 2025](<https://afriqueitnews.com/tech-media/rdc-tanzanie-interconnexion-fibre-optique-pourrait-transformer-region/>), with works due in early 2026. In the last twelve months, the ministries of the country and Uganda [signed a memorandum on 11 May 2026](<https://ict.go.ug/media/news/uganda-and-drc-deepen-digital-and-regional-cooperation>) that includes joining Uganda's backbone to Congolese fibre. Tanzania [reaffirmed the lake cable in September 2026](<https://dailynews.co.tz/tanzania-drc-agree-to-fast-track-sgr-link-and-fibre-optic-cable-across-lake-tanganyika/>). Burundi's Council of Ministers [adopted a memorandum on 8 May 2024](<https://abpinfo.bi/2024/05/15/un-memorandum-dentente-du-projet-dinterconnexion-par-fibre-optique-entre-la-republique-democratique-du-congo-et-le-burundi-a-ete-adopte-au-conseil-des-ministres/>) for a fibre interconnection. No source found says building has started on the links with Burundi, Tanzania or Uganda. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

Under the Central African Backbone, Congo has been interconnected with Gabon since 2018, [a French Treasury sheet](<https://www.tresor.economie.gouv.fr/Pays/CG/le-secteur-du-numerique>) says. The Central African Republic [inaugurated its interconnection with Congo at Bomassa in February 2023](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/infrastructures/0802-105283-inauguration-de-la-dorsale-optique-nationale-de-la-republique-centrafricaine-et-de-l-interconnexion-avec-le-congo>). In the last twelve months, ADIAC [said in August 2026](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/numerique-les-tuyaux-ont-gagne-du-terrain-lusage-cherche-encore-le-sien-171228>) that the backbone's link to Cameroon was still being built. Gabon's SPIN and Cameroon's CAMTEL [signed a memorandum on CAB-Corridor](<https://spin.ga/cab-corridor-spin-camtel-connectivite-afrique-centrale/>), published in October 2026, and no Congolese party to it has been found. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Djibouti Telecom, Ethio telecom and Sudatel signed [a memorandum in Addis Ababa in December 2024](<https://www.ethiotelecom.et/ethio-telecom-djibouti-telecom-and-sudatel-group-sign/>). In the last twelve months, the three [signed an agreement in Djibouti on 4 February 2026](<https://www.lanation.dj/djibouti-telecom-ethio-telecomet-sudatel-telecom-group-signent-un-accord-strategique-pour-linitiative-horizon-fiber/>) to build and maintain Horizon, a fibre corridor of about 2,800 km to Ethiopia and Sudan. In September 2026 they [presented Horizon to carriers before deployment](<https://www.lanation.dj/projet-de-fibre-optique-horizon-une-nouvelle-autoroute-numerique-pour-la-corne-de-lafrique/>). It is not yet in service. No source found says building has started. None names a Somali, Kenyan or Ethiopian party to a cable already working. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

Algeria's ministry [said in July 2024](<https://www.mpt.gov.dz/lalgerie-abrite-la-5eme-session-du-comite-de-liason-de-la-dorsale-transsaharienne-a-fibre-optique/>) that works on its 2,600 km section of the trans-Saharan backbone, from Algiers to In Guezzam, were complete. In the last twelve months, Algérie Télécom and Niger Telecom [signed a convention in Niamey on 8 September 2026](<https://www.lesahel.org/cooperation-niger-telecom-algerie-telecom-un-partenariat-pour-renforcer-les-capacites-des-infrastructures-telecoms-du-niger/>) for a 100 gigabit link. The ministers of Algeria and Niger [opened the trans-Saharan fibre link at Assamaka on 6 October 2026](<https://algerie-eco.com/2026/10/06/lalgerie-et-le-niger-lancent-lexploitation-de-la-dorsale-transsaharienne-a-fibre-optique/>). Niger's ministry [declared it officially in service](<https://mcnti.gouv.ne/souverainete-et-integration-numerique-lancement-de-lexploitation-de-la-liaison-transsaharienne-en-fibre-optique-niger-algerie-a-assamaka/>). No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Egypt's telecommunications minister [launched a 400 km fibre cable to Sudan on 26 October 2004](<https://sudantribune.com/article/6899>), built to carry calls and internet between the two countries. Telecom Egypt and Sudatel [signed a cooperation agreement in April 2021](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/10989-telecom-egypt-and-sudatel-plan-connectivity-cooperation.html>) to make better use of that fibre. They also planned to join Sudatel's Port Sudan landing to Telecom Egypt's Red Sea landings. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement, memorandum or financing for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

A commentary [published on 16 April 2026 says Eritrea still has no international fibre connection](<https://russellsouthwood.substack.com/p/the-long-view-what-ict4d-did-for>). A 2021 World Bank overview [said the planned regional sea cable and data projects lacked a commitment](<https://doi.org/10.1596/36458>) to serve the whole region, Asmara included. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement, financing or start of works on any link to a neighbour has been found, and no regional programme's plans name Eritrea. No link, exchange point or data facility shared with another African country has been found. Preparing would need an agreement made in the past three years, with another African country or through a regional body, to build, join or run shared digital infrastructure.

Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel [signed a tripartite agreement on 4 February 2026](<https://www.ethiotelecom.et/ethio-telecom-djibouti-telecom-and-sudatel-group-sign/>) for Horizon, a fibre corridor from Djibouti's cable landings across Ethiopia to Sudan's. It builds on a memorandum signed in Addis Ababa on 3 December 2024. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 Ethio telecom [moved from planning into active deployment](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/20/ethio-telecom-active-deployment-africa-middle-east-fibre-corridor/>), with its design final and site materials delivered. In September 2026 the three operators [presented Horizon to carriers ahead of commercial launch](<https://www.lanation.dj/projet-de-fibre-optique-horizon-une-nouvelle-autoroute-numerique-pour-la-corne-de-lafrique/>). No source found says a shared link, exchange point or data centre is in service. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

Gabon's and Equatorial Guinea's ministers [inaugurated the interconnection of the Gabonese and Equatoguinean backbones on 10 November 2025](<https://spin.ga/alliance-historique-numerique-gabon-guinee-equatoriale/>), at Meyo-Kyé and Ebebeyin, after [signing an agreement at Mongomo](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/11/13/historic-fibre-roaming-and-frequency-deals-signed-between-gabon-and-equatorial-guinea/>). Tests confirmed traffic flowing between Bitam and Ebebeyin, and between Libreville and Bata. In the last twelve months, Gabon's backbone company SPIN and Cameroon's CAMTEL [signed a memorandum on CAB-Corridor](<https://spin.ga/cab-corridor-spin-camtel-connectivite-afrique-centrale/>), published in October 2026, that would join Cameroon, Gabon and Congo. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

CSquared, the Nigerian operator Phase3 and Benin's state infrastructure company SBIN [announced a fibre route from Lagos to Accra in May 2025](<https://csquared.com/csquared-phase3-and-sbin-commission-lagos-to-accra-terrestrial-fibre-route-strengthening-west-africas-digital-resilience/>), running through Benin and Togo into Ghana. The partners said it was configured, activated and tested, and gave no date for it to enter service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. GVA of Côte d'Ivoire [holds a 100 Gbps port at Accra-IX](<https://tech.africa/accra-three-internet-exchanges/>), routing data of August 2026 show, and CSquared [runs its own network from Accra to Lagos](<https://csquared.com/8208/>). Neither is an arrangement between bodies of two countries. No source found says the route is in service. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

Guinea's telecoms ministry [says four cross-border interconnections were working in 2025](<https://www.africaguinee.com/app/uploads/2026/01/Realisations_MPTEN_2025_compressed.pdf>), with Mali, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and Sierra Leone. Guinea and Sierra Leone [signed an agreement in November 2024](<https://natca.gov.sl/2025/11/17/the-republic-of-sierra-leone-signs-free-roaming-agreement-with-republic-of-guinea-to-ease-cross-border-connectivity/>) to interconnect their national backbones. Guinea's SOGEB and Sierra Leone's Leoncom [then signed an interconnection agreement in Conakry](<https://www.telecomreviewafrica.com/articles/general-news/12188-guinea-and-sierra-leone-link-national-fibre-networks-for-regional-digital-integration/>), published in June 2025. In June 2024 SOGEB and Mali's SMTD [agreed to interconnect the two countries' networks](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/optical-fixed-networks/17258-guinea-adds-cote-d-ivoire-to-regional-fibre-interconnectivity-plan.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Gamtel's company profile, captured in September 2026, [says the state operator holds 28 Gbps with the Senegalese operator Free on Cross Gambia, a backup link](<https://gamtel.gm/about-us/>). The page is undated. Traffic moves onto the link automatically when the ACE sea cable fails. The Gambia also [joined the backbone of WACREN](<https://wacren.net/en/news/wacren-connects-six-new-countries-and-sets-foundation-for-climate-programme/>), the regional research and education network, in 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Guinea-Bissau [joined the backbone of WACREN](<https://wacren.net/en/news/wacren-connects-six-new-countries-and-sets-foundation-for-climate-programme/>), the regional research and education network, in 2025, with five other West African countries. AfricaConnect projects co-funded by the European Commission support the expansion. An ECOWAS commissioner [said a protocol of April 2023 consolidated commitment to the Amilcar Cabral sea cable](<https://ang.gw/telecomunicacoes-ministro-diz-que-o-projeto-do-cabo-submarino-amilcar-cabral-vai-reforcar-a-integracao-da-guine-bissau-ao-mundo-global/>), whose study and construction were still unfunded in June 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Equatorial Guinea's and Gabon's ministers [inaugurated the interconnection of the Gabonese and Equatoguinean backbones on 10 November 2025](<https://spin.ga/alliance-historique-numerique-gabon-guinee-equatoriale/>), at Meyo-Kyé and Ebebeyin. Tests confirmed traffic flowing between Bitam and Ebebeyin, and between Libreville and Bata. In the last twelve months, Nigeria's Backbone Connectivity Network and Equatorial Guinea's transport minister [signed a sea cable agreement in Malabo in February 2026](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/fiber-networking/nigeria-equatorial-guinea-subsea-cable-to-strengthen-regional-connectivity>) for a direct link between the two countries. Specifications, investment and a timetable were not disclosed. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found, and no source says work on the cable to Nigeria has begun. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

TTCL and Kenya's ICT Authority [launched a fibre link between Dar es Salaam and Mombasa in July 2025](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/connectivity/east-african-countries-to-launch-regional-satellite>). Tanzania's [Daily News reported it running at 1.6 terabits a second](<https://dailynews.co.tz/new-fibre-link-to-boost-east-africas-digital-resilience/>), with Kenyan companies using it. In the last twelve months, Uganda and Kenya [completed a fibre connection at Busia](<https://pmldaily.com/news/2026/08/uganda-rwanda-complete-fiber-link-at-mirama-hills-border.html>), PML Daily reported in August 2026. An agreement between NITA-U and the ICT Authority is still to be finalised there. A World Bank report counts [a cross-border connectivity memorandum between Kenya and South Sudan](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099063026190082191/txt/P176181-84d9770b-853c-4bb8-8e5a-996eac681382.txt>) as signed by June 2026. No exchange point or data centre shared with another country under an agreement has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

The METISS consortium states that its 3,200 km sea cable [entered service on 5 March 2021](<https://fibernet.ceb.mu/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/2021-03-17-MISE-EN-SERVICE-DU-CABLE-METISS.pdf>). It links Mauritius, Réunion and Madagascar, landing at Fort Dauphin, to a landing near Durban. Telma is its Malagasy member, beside Mauritius's CEB and Emtel. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement, memorandum or financing for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

In June 2024 Mali's SMTD and Guinea's SOGEB [agreed to interconnect the two countries' fibre networks](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/optical-fixed-networks/17258-guinea-adds-cote-d-ivoire-to-regional-fibre-interconnectivity-plan.html>), with ministry support. In the last twelve months, Senegal's SENUM and SMTD [inaugurated the interconnection of their national backbones at the Kidira and Diboli border on 5 October 2026](<https://aps.sn/bakel-inauguration-de-linterconnexion-des-backbones-du-senegal-et-du-mali/>). The chairman of ROA-BN, the West African network of national backbones, [said in November 2025 that its network is working](<https://guineematin.com/2025/11/11/connectivite-regionale-le-siege-du-reseau-ouest-africain-des-backbones-ouvert-a-conakry/>). Mali is connected to Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea and Senegal within it. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Mozambique's communications minister [launched the interconnectivity project with Zambia at Cassacatiza on 20 February 2026](<https://mznews.co.mz/mocambique-e-zambia-avancam-com-interligacao-digital-transfronteirica-em-chifunde/>), a cross-border fibre partnership of Vodacom Moçambique and Bayobab Zambia. Zambia and Mozambique [officially launched the Chanida to Cassacatiza fibre interconnector](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/zambia-and-mozambique-launch-fibre-optic-interconnector/>), reported on 23 February 2026. In the last twelve months, Mozambique's and Angola's ministers also [signed a memorandum on 22 June 2026](<https://www.oeconomico.com/mocambique-e-angola-avancam-com-cabo-nacala-lobito-para-reforcar-corredor-digital-regional/>) for a sea cable from Nacala to Lobito. It is still at the concession stage. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Mauritania [joined the backbone of WACREN](<https://wacren.net/en/news/wacren-connects-six-new-countries-and-sets-foundation-for-climate-programme/>), the regional research and education network, in 2025, with five other West African countries. AfricaConnect projects co-funded by the European Commission support the expansion, which serves universities and research institutes. WACREN also activated a link from Lagos to Cape Town in the same expansion. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

The METISS consortium states that its 3,200 km sea cable [entered service on 5 March 2021](<https://fibernet.ceb.mu/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/2021-03-17-MISE-EN-SERVICE-DU-CABLE-METISS.pdf>), linking Mauritius, Réunion and Madagascar to a landing near Durban. CEB and Emtel are its Mauritian members, beside Madagascar's Telma. No change has been found in the last twelve months. South African networks [are members of the Mauritius Internet Exchange Point](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/516/>), PeeringDB data of May 2026 show. Foreign members joining an exchange are commercial use. No data facility run with another country has been found, and no exchange point shared under an agreement. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Telecom Namibia, Angola Telecom and the cable company SATCAB [signed a master service agreement on 12 June 2026](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/15/telecom-namibia-angola-telecom-and-satcab-sign-sarssy-deal-to-deliver-1-tbps-connectivity-across-southern-africa/>) joining the Southern African Regional Submarine System to the Equiano cable. In the last twelve months, MTC Namibia and Botswana's BoFiNet [signed a memorandum on 17 February 2026](<https://www.bofinet.co.bw/index.php/news/article/bofinet-signs-mou-with-mtc-namibia-to-further-bolster-connectivity-reliability-for-botswana>) on cross-border fibre. The Angosat-2 work [began as a proof of concept in October 2025](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/connectivity/namibia-taps-angosat-2-to-boost-connectivity>), and Telecom Namibia then [signed a pilot agreement with Angola's space programme office](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/20382-telecom-namibia-signs-satellite-subsea-connectivity-deals-with-angola-firms.html>). No source found says building has begun on the cable work with Angola. None says a shared link, exchange or data centre is in service. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

Niger's minister [received 1,031 km of the trans-Saharan fibre backbone on 14 November 2025](<https://anp.ne/niger-reception-provisoire-des-troncons-du-projet-de-la-dorsale-transsaharienne-a-fibre-optique/>), reaching the Algerian, Chadian, Nigerian, Beninese and Burkinabe borders. In the last twelve months, Niger's and Algeria's ministers [opened the link at Assamaka on 6 October 2026](<https://anp.ne/niger-algerie-lancement-a-assamaka-de-lexploitation-de-la-dorsale-transsaharienne-a-fibre-optique/>). Niger's ministry [declared it officially in service](<https://mcnti.gouv.ne/souverainete-et-integration-numerique-lancement-de-lexploitation-de-la-liaison-transsaharienne-en-fibre-optique-niger-algerie-a-assamaka/>). Algeria reports a capacity of up to 100 gigabits a second from the start. No source found says the links to Chad, Nigeria or Benin are working, or that an exchange point or data centre is shared. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Phase3 and Senegal's Sonatel [activated a 3,500 km fibre route from Lagos to Dakar in May 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/05/09/west-africas-digital-backbone-phase3-and-sonatel-launch-3500km-fibre-route/>), running through Benin, Togo and Ghana. In the last twelve months, Nigeria's Backbone Connectivity Network and Equatorial Guinea's transport minister [signed a sea cable agreement in Malabo in February 2026](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/fiber-networking/nigeria-equatorial-guinea-subsea-cable-to-strengthen-regional-connectivity>). No source reports works begun on it. Phase3, CSquared and Benin's SBIN [announced a fibre route from Lagos to Accra in May 2025](<https://csquared.com/csquared-phase3-and-sbin-commission-lagos-to-accra-terrestrial-fibre-route-strengthening-west-africas-digital-resilience/>), tested but not yet open. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Uganda's head of Northern Corridor projects said in August 2026 that Uganda and Rwanda [made the final fibre connection at the Mirama Hills border](<https://pmldaily.com/news/2026/08/uganda-rwanda-complete-fiber-link-at-mirama-hills-border.html>) earlier in 2026. In the last twelve months, the link was built under the Northern Corridor Integration Projects. Operators on both sides must still agree capacity before it is switched on. Foreign networks [are members of the Rwanda Internet Exchange](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/401/>), which is commercial use. No source found says the Mirama Hills link, or any other shared facility, is in service. No data facility run with another country has been found. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

Egypt's minister [launched a 400 km fibre cable to Sudan on 26 October 2004](<https://sudantribune.com/article/6899>), built to carry calls and internet between the two countries. Telecom Egypt and Sudatel [signed a cooperation agreement in April 2021](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/10989-telecom-egypt-and-sudatel-plan-connectivity-cooperation.html>) to make better use of that fibre. In the last twelve months, Sudatel, Djibouti Telecom and Ethio telecom [signed a tripartite agreement on 4 February 2026](<https://www.lanation.dj/djibouti-telecom-ethio-telecomet-sudatel-telecom-group-signent-un-accord-strategique-pour-linitiative-horizon-fiber/>) for Horizon, a fibre corridor to Sudan. In September 2026 Horizon was [still being presented to carriers before deployment](<https://www.lanation.dj/projet-de-fibre-optique-horizon-une-nouvelle-autoroute-numerique-pour-la-corne-de-lafrique/>). No source reports work begun on the Sudanese section. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Sonatel and Phase3 [activated a fibre route from Dakar to Lagos in May 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/05/09/west-africas-digital-backbone-phase3-and-sonatel-launch-3500km-fibre-route/>). In the last twelve months, SENUM and SMTD [joined their national backbones at the Kidira and Diboli border on 5 October 2026](<https://aps.sn/bakel-inauguration-de-linterconnexion-des-backbones-du-senegal-et-du-mali/>). Gambia's Gamtel [holds 28 Gbps with the Senegalese operator Free on a backup link](<https://gamtel.gm/about-us/>), its profile of September 2026 says. Senegal and Guinea [signed a memorandum in November 2025](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/3141/senegal-and-guinea-sign-digital-cooperation-agreement-at-transform-africa-summit-2025>) to work on joining their telecommunications networks, and no contract or works under it have been found. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Sierra Leone and Guinea [signed an agreement in November 2024](<https://natca.gov.sl/2025/11/17/the-republic-of-sierra-leone-signs-free-roaming-agreement-with-republic-of-guinea-to-ease-cross-border-connectivity/>) to interconnect their national backbones, the regulator NatCA says. Guinea's SOGEB and Sierra Leone's Leoncom [then signed an interconnection agreement in Conakry](<https://www.telecomreviewafrica.com/articles/general-news/12188-guinea-and-sierra-leone-link-national-fibre-networks-for-regional-digital-integration/>), published in June 2025. Guinea's telecoms ministry [lists the interconnection among four working in 2025](<https://www.africaguinee.com/app/uploads/2026/01/Realisations_MPTEN_2025_compressed.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no Sierra Leonean source on its opening has been found. [Michcom-IX](<https://www.michcom-ix.net/>) runs an exchange with points in Freetown, Conakry and Monrovia, but one company runs it, with no agreement between national bodies. No data facility shared with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Somalia is one of five recipients of the World Bank's Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project. A June 2026 status report says it [became effective for all five between 2023 and 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099063026190082191/txt/P176181-84d9770b-853c-4bb8-8e5a-996eac681382.txt>). The [2023 grant agreement](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099062123164542123/pdf/P17618108dc2460600945a0f83353acb3fb.pdf>) pays for cross-border links. In the last twelve months, consultancies have prepared fibre deployment in Somalia and Somaliland, and broadband deployment in Somaliland was expected to start in the second half of 2026. No source found says building has begun on the project's links, or names a Somali party to a working shared cable. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

South Sudan and Kenya [signed an agreement at the EACO assembly in June 2025](<https://au-pida.org/prospectus/project.php?id=18>) for a 2,420 km fibre link into South Sudan. An August 2025 mission said South Sudan [was to tender fibre to the Kenyan and Sudanese borders](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099120225134529047/txt/P176181-10a2aeb5-d3fb-4c67-bc53-da109b62a9de.txt>). In the last twelve months, bids for [397 km on the Juba to Nadapal route](<https://southsudanpress.com/analysis-south-sudan-fibre-juba-nadapal-procurement.html>) closed on 26 October 2026. A World Bank report of June 2026 [counts a cross-border connectivity memorandum between Kenya and South Sudan as signed](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099063026190082191/txt/P176181-84d9770b-853c-4bb8-8e5a-996eac681382.txt>). No source found says a contract was awarded or works began on the fibre to Kenya. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

The national operator CST [joined the ACE cable consortium in 2010](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/234391468190440376/txt/ICR3141-P117652-Box391488B-OUO-9.txt>) by signing its construction and maintenance agreement. The ACE cable [was commercially launched in February 2013](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/234391468190440376/txt/ICR3141-P117652-Box391488B-OUO-9.txt>) after tests across the 16 countries it connects. The segment from Côte d'Ivoire to São Tomé was among those in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement, memorandum or financing for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

No stage is set. An [alternative route through Maputo](<https://uasf.esccom.org.sz/programmes/connectivity-programmes/>) dates from October 2023, and South Africa's [Broadband Infraco](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/broadband-infraco-intensifies-capacity-to-platinum-belt/LPwQ57lynQmMNgkj>) names no Eswatini party. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports shared infrastructure agreed in the last three years or in service, and none says the country has none. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says Eswatini shares no digital infrastructure with another African country.

Chad told ITU-D in March 2026 that its [35 km link from N'Djamena to Cameroon is working](<https://www.itu.int/md/D26-SG01-C-0040/en>), interconnected with the network of CAMTEL, Cameroon's state operator. Chad's operator SOTEL [has bought capacity from CAMTEL over it since 2015](<https://www.sikafinance.com/marches/le-tchad-securise-sa-connectivite-avec-le-cameroun-par-un-nouvel-accord-sur-la-fibre-optique_52735>). Chad's section of the trans-Saharan backbone [started works in 2023](<https://tchadinfos.com/2026/01/11/projet-dorsale-transsaharienne-des-degradations-constatees-sur-le-site-technique-de-bol/>), and in the last twelve months it was [60% complete in February 2026](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1302-52879-chad-plans-50-telecom-sites-50-km-of-fiber-in-n-djamena>). A planned operator route to Cameroon [was suspended by the regulator](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/fiber-networking/chad-tells-operators-to-fast-track-fiber-link-to-cameroon>) in February 2026. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

CSquared, the Nigerian operator Phase3 and Benin's state infrastructure company SBIN [announced a fibre route from Lagos to Accra in May 2025](<https://csquared.com/csquared-phase3-and-sbin-commission-lagos-to-accra-terrestrial-fibre-route-strengthening-west-africas-digital-resilience/>), running through Benin and Togo into Ghana. The partners said it was configured, activated and tested, and gave no date for it to enter service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No Togolese public body has been found as a party to the route. An Ivorian network [holds a port at the Lomé exchange TGIX](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/677/>), PeeringDB data of July 2026 show, and a foreign member joining an exchange is commercial use. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

Tunisian and Algerian delegations on their joint technical commission [agreed on 6 June 2026 to upgrade the land link between the two countries](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0806-56258-algeria-tunisia-plan-new-submarine-cable-to-expand-digital-connectivity-with-europe>). The same commission discussed a new sea cable to Europe. In the last twelve months, the two countries agreed this upgrade, and the source names no contract or start of works, no capacity and no date for it. It calls the land link existing but gives no date or terms for it. No link, exchange point or data facility in service under a named arrangement has been found. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

TTCL and Kenya's ICT Authority [launched a fibre link between Dar es Salaam and Mombasa in July 2025](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/connectivity/east-african-countries-to-launch-regional-satellite>), and the two governments [officially opened the route at Horohoro](<https://dailynews.co.tz/new-fibre-link-to-boost-east-africas-digital-resilience/>). TTCL says it runs at 1.6 terabits a second. In the last twelve months, Tanzania [reaffirmed the Kalemie to Kigoma lake cable with Congo in September 2026](<https://dailynews.co.tz/tanzania-drc-agree-to-fast-track-sgr-link-and-fibre-optic-cable-across-lake-tanganyika/>). On 18 August 2026 its communications ministry [reported the Kigoma end of the link 5 per cent built](<https://www.mawasiliano.go.tz/news/naibu-waziri-mkama-akagua-mradi-wa-mkongo-wa-taifa-kuunganisha-tanzania-na-drc>), with completion expected in April 2027. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

Uganda and Rwanda [made the final fibre connection at the Mirama Hills border](<https://pmldaily.com/news/2026/08/uganda-rwanda-complete-fiber-link-at-mirama-hills-border.html>) earlier in 2026, under the Northern Corridor Integration Projects. In the last twelve months, the same report says, Uganda and Kenya completed a connection at Busia, and an agreement between NITA-U and Kenya's ICT Authority is still to be finalised there. On 11 May 2026 Uganda's ICT ministry and the Congolese telecoms ministry [signed a memorandum](<https://ict.go.ug/media/news/uganda-and-drc-deepen-digital-and-regional-cooperation>), one of whose projects joins Uganda's backbone to Congolese fibre. NITA-U and Tanzania's TTCL [signed a memorandum on 29 September 2023](<https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/questions-swirl-over-internet-deal-between-uganda-tanzania-5654914>). No source found says a shared link is in service. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

Mozambique's research network MoRENet [has a border point in Cape Town](<https://africarxiv.ubuntunet.net/bitstreams/9427cb02-feef-4b3f-b03b-84cb4efea3cb/download>), connected to South Africa's research networks TENET and SANReN. It carries Mozambique's international capacity of 60 Gbps, and was described as operational in October 2025. [That month WACREN announced a 10 Gbps link from Lagos to the ZAOXI exchange point in Cape Town](<https://wacren.net/en/newsletter/africas-research-and-education-networks-achieve-historic-lagos-cape-town-interconnection/>), through the same networks. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service, such as an exchange point or data centre shared under an agreement between national bodies.

In January 2025 a World Bank document [said cross-border infrastructure was missing](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099012025023033676/txt/P505094-630a5ef9-d23a-4221-b7c8-397c94a90b4d.txt>) in Zambia, hindering digital trade. In the last twelve months, Zambia and Mozambique [commissioned the Chanida to Cassacatiza fibre interconnector](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/zambia-and-mozambique-launch-fibre-optic-interconnector/>), reported on 23 February 2026. It joins Zambia's national backbone to Mozambique's sea cable network. Zambia's science and technology minister [attended the launch of the project with Mozambique on 20 February 2026](<https://mznews.co.mz/mocambique-e-zambia-avancam-com-interligacao-digital-transfronteirica-em-chifunde/>). No exchange point or data centre shared with another country has been found, No report that building has started on the Lake Tanganyika cable to Burundi has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

No stage is set. The [Powertel and Paratus fibre corridor](<https://paratus.africa/blog/paratus-zimbabwe-and-powertel-switch-on-new-digital-highway/>) is a partnership inside Zimbabwe, and the [Harare internet exchange point](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Regional-Presence/Africa/Documents/2020/contributions/RI2_POTRAZ-Zimbabwe-IXP_RDFAFR2020.pdf>) is a further source. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports shared infrastructure agreed in the last three years, or in service under an agreement, and none says the country has none. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says Zimbabwe shares no digital infrastructure with another African country.
